If you missed the desk at  in Hoboken (1450 Bloomfield St), your reservation isn't automatically dead—Avis holds reservations for up to 24 hours past your scheduled pick-up time if you are delayed, provided you call to let them know (Avis Location Services FAQ).

What happens to your booking and fees

Reservation hold: Because Avis honors delayed pickups for up to 24 hours, you can still pick up your car when the Hoboken branch opens (Sunday at 8:00 AM; Mon–Fri 7:30 AM–7:00 PM, Sat 8:00 AM–4:00 PM), as long as an agent notes the delay on your reservation.

No-show fees (if you don't pick up or call): Per Avis's Reservations FAQ, Pay at Counter bookings with no card hold have no fee. If you booked with a credit card hold, a $75 no-show fee applies if not canceled at least 24 hours ahead; Prepaid ("Pay Now") bookings carry a $150 fee for a no-show or cancellation within 24 hours (versus $50 outside 24 hours).

Your President's Club leverage: You get access to a dedicated support line (listed in the Avis app under your Preferred profile) and priority handling (Avis Preferred). While the President's Club guaranteed-car perk requires booking 24 hours in advance (Upgraded Points), an agent can usually waive a no-show fee or transfer your reservation to a 24-hour location right now.

What to do right now
1
Call Avis immediately
Use your President's Club line in the Avis app, or 1-800-633-3469

Tell the agent you missed the Hoboken counter closing and want them to note a late pickup on your confirmation number so the system doesn't cancel it as a no-show.

2
Choose between waiting for Hoboken or switching to a 24-hour branch

If you can wait until 8:00 AM Sunday, keep the Hoboken pickup. If you need a car tonight or early morning, ask the agent to transfer your reservation to Newark Liberty International Airport or Midtown East in Manhattan.

3
Ask to preserve your rate and waive any modification fee

Mention your President's Club status and ask them to apply your existing rate (or waive any no-show/rebooking penalty) if you switch locations.

4
Confirm the updated pickup details in the Avis app

Before heading out, verify that the new pickup time or branch address shows in your app so your vehicle assignment is ready when you arrive.

turns.response:
No —  at 1450 Bloomfield St (Hudson Tea Parking Garage) does not allow after-hours returns and has no key drop box.

Per Avis's location policy for Hudson Tea Parking Garage, vehicles must be returned during office hours (Sunday 8:00 AM–6:00 PM, Mon–Fri 7:30 AM–7:00 PM, Sat 8:00 AM–4:00 PM). Avis explicitly warns not to park the car and lock or leave the keys inside—you remain responsible for the vehicle, all ongoing rental charges, any theft or damage, and any locksmith fees.

Your two options right now

Keep the car until Hoboken opens at 8:00 AM Sunday (usually cheapest):

Call 1-800-230-4898 (or your President's Club line in the Avis app) right away to report the late return so your rental is officially extended (Avis Reservations FAQ). If you don't notify Avis within 7 hours of your scheduled return time, a late fee of up to $15/day can apply on top of the extra rental time.

For time past your 24-hour rental window, Avis charges an hourly rate (three-fourths of the daily rate plus $0.01 on daily/weekend rates, or half the daily rate plus $0.01 on weekly rates) up to a full extra day (Avis Rental Car Return FAQ). As a President's Club member, ask the agent—or the Hoboken counter manager when you hand over the keys at 8:00 AM—if they can waive the late/extension fee as a courtesy.

Return it tonight to a 24-hour airport location:

Avis's stated fallback when a branch lacks a drop box is changing your drop-off to the nearest regional airport (Avis Hoboken H8K)—for you, that's  at Newark Liberty International Airport (132 Carson Rd, Newark, NJ, open 24 hours).

Call 1-800-230-4898 or your President's Club line first before driving there so they update the drop-off location on your agreement and tell you whether a one-way/drop-off modification fee applies (it's often cheaper to just wait until 8:00 AM in Hoboken than to pay a last-minute one-way fee plus an Uber back from Newark).

turns.prompt: Keeping it till morning to avoid Newark fees; check Palisade Ave Union city and Hudson Tea overnight parking rules, plus waiving extra-day fees for traffic and app errors.
turns.response:
Parking inside Hudson Tea Garage is your safest bet tonight—Union City enforces a city-wide overnight permit rule, so leaving a rental car on Palisade Ave overnight risks a $60 ticket.

Overnight parking: Palisade Ave (Union City) vs. Hudson Tea Garage

Palisade Ave, Union City (Risky without a permit): Per the Union City Parking Authority, a residential or visitor permit is required city-wide from 10:00 PM to 7:00 AM (violations carry a $60 fine per the UCPA Violations Schedule). Unless you have a Union City visitor permit hangtag, don't park on Palisade Ave overnight—even though daytime meters aren't enforced on Sundays.

Hudson Tea Garage —  (Safest): Located right at 1450 Bloomfield St (+1 201-795-5285), the public garage is open 24/7 and puts the car in the same building as the Avis counter for your 8:00 AM drop-off.

Where to park: Pull a regular ticket at the gate or book ahead on SpotHero (often around $12 depending on hours; scan the QR code instead of pulling a ticket if using SpotHero).

What to avoid: Park only in non-reserved spaces—do not park in spots marked "Reserved" or "AVIS Parking Only" (SpotHero Facility Rules), as leaving an unreturned car in an Avis-only bay overnight doesn't close your contract and risks towing.

Waiving extra-day fees for traffic and app errors

Avis's standard policy charges hourly late fees (three-fourths of the daily rate plus $0.01 per hour on daily/weekend rates) up to an extra day once you pass your 24-hour window, plus up to $15/day if you don't call 1-800-230-4898 to extend (Avis Reservations FAQ; Avis Rental Car Return FAQ). Because 1450 Bloomfield has no drop box, here is how to maximize your chances of getting the extra charges waived as a President's Club member:

                text {
                  text: "The Weehawken waterfront, nestled along the New Jersey side of the Hudson River, is a hidden gem that offers an unrivaled perspective of the iconic New York City skyline. My recent visit to this picturesque locale left me captivated, and I am eager to share the enchanting details of this experience in a comprehensive Google review.\n\nThe standout feature of the Weehawken waterfront is undoubtedly the breathtaking view it affords. Positioned directly across from Manhattan, the skyline appears almost magical from this vantage point. The cityscape, adorned with towering skyscrapers and illuminated bridges, takes on an ethereal quality, especially as the sun sets and the city lights come to life. The contrast of the serene waters of the Hudson River against the vibrant city lights creates a scene that is nothing short of mesmerizing.\n\nThe view from the Jersey side, particularly at night, transforms New York City into a dazzling spectacle. The twinkling lights of the city that never sleeps reflect on the water, creating a shimmering panorama. The skyline, with landmarks like the Empire State Building and One World Trade Center standing tall, becomes a work of art that unfolds before your eyes. There's an undeniable charm to witnessing the city's energy from a distance, providing a unique perspective that amplifies its grandeur.\n\nExploring the Weehawken waterfront further reveals a well-designed space that invites locals and visitors alike to savor the breathtaking surroundings. The waterfront park offers a peaceful escape, with well-maintained paths for leisurely strolls, benches strategically placed for contemplation, and green spaces that invite relaxation. The ambiance is perfect for both quiet reflection and vibrant social gatherings, making it a versatile destination for individuals, couples, and families.\n\nAs someone who appreciates photography, the Weehawken waterfront proved to be a haven for capturing stunning cityscapes. The unobstructed views and varied perspectives make it an ideal location for photographers seeking to encapsulate the dynamic beauty of New York City. Whether you're an amateur capturing the scenery with a smartphone or a professional with sophisticated equipment, the waterfront provides an ideal canvas for creative expression.\n\nIn summary, the Weehawken waterfront stands as a testament to the understated beauty found just across the river from New York City. The awe-inspiring view, especially at night, transforms the skyline into a spectacle that is both calming and invigorating. The well-designed public spaces, combined with the natural beauty of the Hudson River, create an environment that is ideal for relaxation and appreciation of urban splendor. If you're seeking a unique perspective of New York City that showcases its splendor from a distance, the Weehawken waterfront is a destination that promises an unforgettable experience."
                  language_code: "en"

                          rating: 5.0
                          text {
                            text: "The Weehawken waterfront, nestled along the New Jersey side of the Hudson River, is a hidden gem that offers an unrivaled perspective of the iconic New York City skyline. My recent visit to this picturesque locale left me captivated, and I am eager to share the enchanting details of this experience in a comprehensive Google review.\n\nThe standout feature of the Weehawken waterfront is undoubtedly the breathtaking view it affords. Positioned directly across from Manhattan, the skyline appears almost magical from this vantage point. The cityscape, adorned with towering skyscrapers and illuminated bridges, takes on an ethereal quality, especially as the sun sets and the city lights come to life. The contrast of the serene waters of the Hudson River against the vibrant city lights creates a scene that is nothing short of mesmerizing.\n\nThe view from the Jersey side, particularly at night, transforms New York City into a dazzling spectacle. The twinkling lights of the city that never sleeps reflect on the water, creating a shimmering panorama. The skyline, with landmarks like the Empire State Building and One World Trade Center standing tall, becomes a work of art that unfolds before your eyes. There's an undeniable charm to witnessing the city's energy from a distance, providing a unique perspective that amplifies its grandeur.\n\nExploring the Weehawken waterfront further reveals a well-designed space that invites locals and visitors alike to savor the breathtaking surroundings. The waterfront park offers a peaceful escape, with well-maintained paths for leisurely strolls, benches strategically placed for contemplation, and green spaces that invite relaxation. The ambiance is perfect for both quiet reflection and vibrant social gatherings, making it a versatile destination for individuals, couples, and families.\n\nAs someone who appreciates photography, the Weehawken waterfront proved to be a haven for capturing stunning cityscapes. The unobstructed views and varied perspectives make it an ideal location for photographers seeking to encapsulate the dynamic beauty of New York City. Whether you're an amateur capturing the scenery with a smartphone or a professional with sophisticated equipment, the waterfront provides an ideal canvas for creative expression.\n\nIn summary, the Weehawken waterfront stands as a testament to the understated beauty found just across the river from New York City. The awe-inspiring view, especially at night, transforms the skyline into a spectacle that is both calming and invigorating. The well-designed public spaces, combined with the natural beauty of the Hudson River, create an environment that is ideal for relaxation and appreciation of urban splendor. If you're seeking a unique perspective of New York City that showcases its splendor from a distance, the Weehawken waterfront is a destination that promises an unforgettable experience."
